# Requirements Catalog — S07 Requirements and search (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase A; plateau psa; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d2c-7322-b2f9-4dd041153894; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Fourteen requirements, all must: the five-table schema with tenancy and trigonometry indexes, the 32 registry-declared actions, kind fixed at declaration, the supersede invariant, one revision per mutation, a Rust compare, an idempotent catalogue import, an advisory quality rubric, three ranked search arms, a 40-query human-labelled eval with explicit targets, a single trace-link writer, an idempotent project-request intake, the outbox events and the plan §7 gate itself.

## Links

Derives from the slice plan §5.1–§5.8 and §7; realizes the Phase A requirements view; reuses S03's schema and tenancy conventions and S04's registry contract rather than restating them.

## Document

The artefact sits under the slice plan; each requirement's acceptance is exercised by one of search_index, s07_assets, s07_requests, s07_store, s07_seed, s07_governance or search_eval, and the record-level instrument is acceptance/programme/S07.toml. The published evidence page is 01a1e687-4d95-70a0-8cf9-a624a30dcb36.

entries.axis_b: Five §5.1 tables with full tenancy and the trigram indexes

value.acceptance: tenant_id NOT NULL and ENABLE plus FORCE row-level security with the tenant_isolation policy on every table; quality_evaluation is append-only; pg_trgm and gin(title gin_trgm_ops) on governed_asset and card plus gin(label) on catalogue_entry. outline and outline_node shipped in 0007 and were dropped by 0011.

entries.axis_b: Thirty-two actions over one registry

value.acceptance: requirements.*, principles.*, decisions.*, catalogues.list|import, quality.score, search.query, trace_links.* and project_requests.* are declared through the S04 ActionSpec derive; routes are unversioned /api/<resource>.

entries.axis_b: Kind is fixed by the action name, never by input

value.acceptance: requirements.* is bound to kind='requirement' at declaration and cannot reach a principle; domain::governance::transition(kind, from, to) is the only legality check and is proptested.

entries.axis_b: A superseded asset names its successor in the same statement

value.acceptance: the migration enforces status <> 'superseded' or superseded_by_id is not null, so a transition to superseded without a successor fails loudly.

entries.axis_b: One revision row per mutation in the same transaction

value.acceptance: entity_type='governed_asset', seq = governed_asset.version, label in created|updated|status:<to>, content is the post-mutation snapshot and content_hash is SHA-256 of JCS-canonical JSON; uq(tenant, entity_type, entity_id, seq) refuses a double write.

entries.axis_b: requirements.compare diffs two revisions in Rust

value.acceptance: field-level added/removed/changed over the two content documents, with acceptance matched by criterion id rather than array index, returning RevisionDiff.

entries.axis_b: Catalogue import is idempotent per tenant

value.acceptance: seed/catalogue.json is a checked-in export, never called at runtime; migrate --seed imports it for all tenants by default; a second run returns {0,0,N}; card_type stays its own table while every other line is a catalogue_entry kind.

entries.axis_b: Quality scoring is read-only and advisory

value.acceptance: rubric v1 weights clarity .20, testability .30, atomicity .20, traceability .15 and uniqueness .15; scoring writes only quality_evaluation, never the asset, and runs as a post-commit job with dedupe_key revision:<id>; re-scoring the same revision yields the same number.

entries.axis_b: Three ranked arms with SQL-side predicates

value.acceptance: governed_asset, card and catalogue_entry are UNION ALL arms each carrying its own LIMIT, with an outer ORDER BY score, id; tenant, kind, status and project predicates are SQL so Rust sees at most limit+1 rows; ts_headline is capped at 50.

entries.axis_b: A human-labelled 40-query eval set with explicit targets

value.acceptance: tests/eval/search_queries.json holds 40 queries across exact_key, title, body_phrase, paraphrase and typo with at least six each; expected ids are human-labelled; targets are recall@5 ≥ 0.75, MRR ≥ 0.60 and B ≥ C, with pgvector (D) shipped when the loss exceeds 0.05 or C is unreachable and B fails A + 0.20.

entries.axis_b: trace_links.* is the only writer of trace_link

value.acceptance: a requirement-to-card link reads back from both the requirement with include=trace and the card's traces endpoint, in the same tenant, with zero cross-tenant rows.

entries.axis_b: Project requests are idempotent and promote atomically

value.acceptance: project_requests are unique on (tenant, external_ref), move through draft, approved, rejected and promoted, and promote creates its project through the store in the same transaction rather than re-calling projects.create.

entries.axis_b: Every mutation writes one outbox event in its transaction

value.acceptance: eleven event types cover governed_asset.created/updated/transitioned/superseded, quality.evaluated, catalogue.imported and the four project_request transitions plus promoted, with the payload keys fixed in plan §5.8.

entries.axis_b: The plan §7 gate names its targets and its index

value.acceptance: the six API and store test targets, the ignored search_eval run and the EXPLAIN block that greps governed_asset_tsv_idx or governed_asset_title_trgm_idx; search_index asserts the index by name as conveyor_runtime.

entries.axis_b: forced row-level security on every new table

value.usage: each S07 table carries tenant_id NOT NULL with ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant_isolation policy using both USING and WITH CHECK, following S03's convention; quality_evaluation is append-only.

entries.axis_b: text plus CHECK constraints

value.usage: status, kind and verdict are text columns constrained by CHECK rather than native enums, so a new value is a migration, not an ALTER TYPE; governed_asset status is draft, in_review, approved or superseded.

entries.axis_b: a generated tsv with a literal english config

value.usage: the tsvector column names 'english' literally because current_setting is not immutable; ts_rank_cd must name the same configuration or it scores zero.

entries.axis_b: pg_trgm beside full text, never instead of it

value.usage: gin(title gin_trgm_ops) serves %, ILIKE and similarity(); tsv @@ tsquery needs gin(tsv); similarity ordering without a % predicate scans the table and is refused.

entries.axis_b: scripts/db-roles.sql marks the operators

value.usage: ts_match_vq and word_similarity_op must be LEAKPROOF or both GINs are dead under FORCE RLS; the plan records the 2026-11-08 measurement where the degraded plan satisfied a loose grep and the check was tightened.

entries.axis_b: RFC 8785 JCS with SHA-256

value.usage: revision.content_hash is the SHA-256 of the JCS-canonical post-mutation snapshot, so equal documents hash equally and a diff is over content, not storage order.

entries.axis_b: unversioned /api/<resource> through the registry

value.usage: all 32 operations are registry-declared actions with unversioned host routes; the durable name is the action, and RM's unprefixed mounts get no alias or rewrite.

entries.axis_b: one event per mutation in the transaction

value.usage: eleven internal event types are written in the mutation's transaction; event names are internal vocabulary and no consumer's naming is copied into the schema.

entries.axis_b: quality scoring outside the mutation lock

value.usage: quality.score runs as job(kind='quality.score', dedupe_key='revision:<id>') after commit; several trigram queries inside the mutation would hold the asset row lock, which the plan refuses.

entries.axis_b: one committed constant, grid-tuned

value.usage: the three search weights are one constant tuned by a bounded grid search, not a learned model; pgvector ships only on the §5.6 trigger.

entries.axis_b: GitHub-hosted preflight and a named index

value.usage: compile and test are answered by the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight, never a local compiling cargo; search_index asserts the GIN by name as conveyor_runtime under enable_seqscan=off.

entries.axis_b: Five §5.1 tables with full tenancy and the trigram indexes

value.acceptance: tenant_id NOT NULL and ENABLE plus FORCE row-level security with the tenant_isolation policy on every table; quality_evaluation is append-only; pg_trgm and gin(title gin_trgm_ops) on governed_asset and card plus gin(label) on catalogue_entry. outline and outline_node shipped in 0007 and were dropped by 0011.

value.acceptance: requirements.*, principles.*, decisions.*, catalogues.list|import, quality.score, search.query, trace_links.* and project_requests.* are declared through the S04 ActionSpec derive; routes are unversioned /api/<resource>.

entries.axis_b: Kind is fixed by the action name, never by input

value.acceptance: requirements.* is bound to kind='requirement' at declaration and cannot reach a principle; domain::governance::transition(kind, from, to) is the only legality check and is proptested.

entries.axis_b: A superseded asset names its successor in the same statement

value.acceptance: the migration enforces status <> 'superseded' or superseded_by_id is not null, so a transition to superseded without a successor fails loudly.

entries.axis_b: One revision row per mutation in the same transaction

value.acceptance: entity_type='governed_asset', seq = governed_asset.version, label in created|updated|status:<to>, content is the post-mutation snapshot and content_hash is SHA-256 of JCS-canonical JSON; uq(tenant, entity_type, entity_id, seq) refuses a double write.

entries.axis_b: requirements.compare diffs two revisions in Rust

value.acceptance: field-level added/removed/changed over the two content documents, with acceptance matched by criterion id rather than array index, returning RevisionDiff.

entries.axis_b: Catalogue import is idempotent per tenant

value.acceptance: seed/catalogue.json is a checked-in export, never called at runtime; migrate --seed imports it for all tenants by default; a second run returns {0,0,N}; card_type stays its own table while every other line is a catalogue_entry kind.

entries.axis_b: Quality scoring is read-only and advisory

entries.axis_b: Three ranked arms with SQL-side predicates

value.acceptance: governed_asset, card and catalogue_entry are UNION ALL arms each carrying its own LIMIT, with an outer ORDER BY score, id; tenant, kind, status and project predicates are SQL so Rust sees at most limit+1 rows; ts_headline is capped at 50.

value.acceptance: a requirement-to-card link reads back from both the requirement with include=trace and the card's traces endpoint, in the same tenant, with zero cross-tenant rows.

entries.axis_b: Project requests are idempotent and promote atomically

value.acceptance: project_requests are unique on (tenant, external_ref), move through draft, approved, rejected and promoted, and promote creates its project through the store in the same transaction rather than re-calling projects.create.

entries.axis_b: Every mutation writes one outbox event in its transaction

value.acceptance: eleven event types cover governed_asset.created/updated/transitioned/superseded, quality.evaluated, catalogue.imported and the four project_request transitions plus promoted, with the payload keys fixed in plan §5.8.

entries.axis_b: The plan §7 gate names its targets and its index
